messages.subject: Congratulations on your camtrapR and a query. Can I use my two files similar to your recordTableSample and camtraps?
parts:
Juergen
Congratulations and thanks for your team’s effort producing camtrapR.  It will be most useful.

I have 380 000 images for 400 sites and 20 mammals.  But I have used ExifPRO to export the species ID and other tags and generate two files similar to your recordTableSample and camtraps.  If I adjust my data to your format, will I be able use such files to complete the rest of workflow you have provided for us.  Or do your two file refer back to the original images - which I’m my case do not exist in locations as you have set up?

Thanks again for a great contribution.
Regards
David

messages.subject: Re: Congratulations on your camtrapR and a query. Can I use my two files similar to your recordTableSample and camtraps?
parts:
Hi David,

you should be able to use your tables given they are in the correct format.

The minimum requirements for the recordTable are: Station ID, species ID, Date/Time (in other words, where was which species seen at which time?).

For the camera trap table, station ID (also camera ID if > 1 camera per station), setup and retrieval date are required. If cameras malfunctioned during the survey, also two columns specifying those periods can be supplied.

 

Station IDs must match between the two tables, and the station column name of both tables must match too.

 

More details on the latter are here:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/ImageOrganisation.html#camera-trap-station-information

 

The file paths are merely for information purposes, to know which image an entry in the table refers to.

 

Best regards,

Jürgen
